item.title: NFL Week 2 picks, predictions: Can the Giants upset the Rams?
item.description: Big Blue View staff weighs in on this week’s NFL games.
item.content:encoded:
The New York Giants seek an improbable 2-0 start when they travel to the West Coast to face the Los Angeles Rams on Monday Night Football. Can they get it? Here is how the Big Blue View staff is picking that game, and the rest of the Week 2 slate.

Chris Pflum

Can the Giants get off to an actual winning streak to start the 2026 season?

I think they can. I do think it’s possible for the Giants to go out to LA and come back with a 2-0 record.

I just don’t think it’s likely.

The way they won against the Cowboys is sustainable and I think both the offense and defense can continue to improve as the players settle into the new schemes. The length and athleticism of the Giants’ defense makes them better equipped than most to counter Sean McVay’s 13-personnel passing attack. The offense has significant untapped potential as players like Darnell Mooney, Odell Beckham Jr., Theo Johnson, and the various running backs become more involved as pass catchers. That, in turn, will make the running game that much more effective.

But I don’t know that it’ll happen in time to survive a shootout with Matt Stafford.

I don’t necessarily buy that the Rams will be out for blood after being embarrassed by the 49ers, but this is a veteran and extremely well schemed offense. They came out flat in week 1, but this offense led the NFL in yards, points, and touchdowns last year. And despite being worse on 3rd downs than the Giants were last year, they still led the NFL in first downs.

The Rams also have a talented and veteran defense with an experienced defensive coordinator. The Rams’ linebackers may be vulnerable the Giants’ passes over the middle, but I’d be surprised if we saw the same level of confusion in the Rams’ back seven as we saw with Dallas.

(As an aside, I find myself shocked at the hubris from Giants’ fans with respect to Aaron Donald. He may have been out of football for two years, but he was still the best defensive tackle in the NFL when he retired, and he has two fewer years of wear and tear on his body than the similarly-aged Shelby Harris.)

Ultimately, I think this game is much closer than the 7.5-point spread and the Giants give the Rams all they can handle. But they don’t have quite enough to stun the NFL and hand LA an 0-2 start to the year.

Pick: Rams

Tony DelGenio

To me, the Rams are one of four NFC teams that could possibly reach the Super Bowl. After sleep-walking through their game in Melbourne and watching the Giants beat up the Cowboys, you can bet they’ll be ready. Some day Matthew Stafford’s NFL clock will hit 12 and he’ll no longer be great. Maybe the the 49ers game was the start of that, maybe not. Against the Giants’ still suspect secondary, and with Puka Nacua and Davante Adams catching passes, I wouldn’t bet on it. Maybe after two years away from the game, Aaron Donald won’t dominate the way he used to. Or maybe he’ll plead with Chris Shula to line him up in the left B-gap where Jon Runyan Jr. will have to deal with him and Andrew Thomas will have to help out. Be alert, Jaxson Dart.

That said, any team that played as well as the Giants did Sunday night has a chance. The Rams’ defensive line is less impressive against the run than the pass, and we saw what the Giants’ running game can do in Week 1. The Giants probably want to be run-heavy again and not test LA cornerbacks Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson too often. The Rams’ offensive line is no longer as formidable as it used to be, and perhaps this is a week where the pass rush can get home against a QB who is not especially mobile. Whether the Giants’ IDL can hold up against Kyren Williams and Blake Corum is a different question. I won’t be shocked if the Giants win this game…but I’m not picking them to do so.

Pick: Rams

Nick Falato

The Giants shocked the world with a home upset over the Dallas Cowboys. Conversely, the Rams were upset in Australia against the San Francisco 49ers. The Giants are currently seven-point dogs, and I expect them to cover the spread, but I expect the Rams to win. Sean McVay will run DUO out of 12/13 personnel, and I think it could wear the Giants down, especially when D.J.

Reader is not on the field. If the Rams are successful running the ball, the play action with Puka Nacau and Davante Adams will become a big issue for the Giants’ cornerbacks. I’m also concerned about Terrance Ferguson off 13 personnel play-action shots; this is, of course, if Kyren Williams and Blake Corum get going against the run. The upgrade at linebackers for the Giants should make them respectable against the run, but I expect the Rams to lean into it and ultimatley have success. The Giants are not the Giants of old, but I have the Rams here.

Pick: Rams by 6

James Hickey

A Giants weakness became a much bigger concern this week when three of the top four cornerbacks appeared on the injury report this week— which led the team to sign two cornerbacks this week.

This comes on a week the team faces arguably the best passing offense in the NFL — Matt Stafford at the helm, with Puka Nacua or Davante Adams as his two top weapons. If that sounds familiar to last week, well the X-factor is that Sean McVay was not on the other sideline.

The headline this week is the expected return of DT Aaron Donald to a defense that gave up the fourth-most rushing yards in the league in Week 1. The Rams allowed 174 yards on the ground and 379 total yards to the 49ers, surrendering 24 unanswered points over the final 35 minutes. On top of that, Myles Garrett, the reigning DPOY, for at least the next four games due to knee surgery.

The Rams are the Super Bowl favorites for a reason. In order to win, the Giants will need to do more in their passing game as they build on their physical running was their key to beating Dallas on Sunday night. While the issues in the secondary are a major red flag, John Harbaugh’s Big Blue Bullies find a way to win on Monday night with a late field goal by rookie Dominic Zvada sailing through the upright for the win.

Pick: Giants 27, Rams 24

David Hartman

Week 1 went just about as well as it could have for John Harbaugh’s Giants, and as terribly as it could have for Sean McVay’s Rams. Much has been made of L.A.’s travel decision for its Australia game, and the team should be rested, and primed for a bounce back in what’s suddenly a very important game for one of the top Super Bowl hopefuls.

The Rams are a 7.5-point favorite and I will gladly take the points. In fact, I think Big Blue is going to give them all they want. I don’t want to overreact to Week 1, and maybe the travel was a big factor, but Los Angeles looked old, and the Giants looked hungry, focused, and sharp.

Los Angeles has much better personnel on defense than Dallas, even without Myles Garrett. New York’s offense controlled the game (and the clock) on Sunday night and this will be a much sterner test. I think they’re ready for it.

I’m taking the upset. I don’t think the top-heavy Rams are as good as advertised, while the Giants might be a little better than people think. New York catches the Rams at the right time, and leaves them in panic mode as they stare down 0-2.

Pick: Giants by 4

Valentine’s View

The New York Giants got the attention of everyone around the NFL with their Week 1 victory over the Dallas Cowboys. There was nothing fluky about the victory, the Giants were the better team on Sunday night. They deserved to win.

The Giants took a huge leap in NFL power rankings, and there are now a lot of bandwagon-jumpers suddenly predicting that John Harbaugh’s team will make the playoffs this season.

Conversely, after an embarrassing Week 1 loss to the San Francisco 49ers, there are people wondering if they were too enamored with the still Super Bowl favorite Rams.

No one should forget that Week 1 of the NFL season is always rife with overreactions. The Rams are still a very good football team that will win a lot of games, almost certainly go to the playoffs, and perhaps reach the Super Bowl. The Giants, good vibes and all, are still a team with much to prove. Oh, and they are traveling across the country to face the in Week 2.

Do I believe that what we saw from the Giants in Week 1 is real? Yes. Do I think the Giants are capable of going to Los Angeles, playing well, and upsetting the Rams? Yes. What I can’t believe is that the Rams will fall to 0-2. The Rams will be at home, Aaron Donald will probably be playing, and they will have desperation on their side.

Pick: Rams

item.title: Sean McVay hopes Rams never play in Australia 'ever again'
item.description: McVay enjoyed the atmosphere Down Under, but is happy to return to a normal schedule of preparation.
item.content:encoded:
It would make Sean McVay very happy if the Los Angeles Rams avoided playing in Australia again while he is head coach.

The Rams' much-talked-abouttrip Down Under ended in a 27-7 defeat to the San Francisco 49ers last week. It was a game to forget for McVay.

"I want to see us be present right now and move forward," McVay said Thursday. "That game is so far — it's almost like you try to do the ‘Men in Black’ thing where you say, 'Hey, I don't remember what happened. That was so long ago.' We're not playing in Australia ever again, I hope. Not because it wasn't a great atmosphere, that'll get taken out of context."

There were over 100,000 fans in attendance at the Melbourne Cricket Ground for the NFL's first-ever regular season game in Australia. It won't be the last time the league makes the trip as Brett Gosper, the NFL's head of Europe and Asia-Pacific, told the Australian Financial Review that there will be at least two more games over the next three seasons.

As McVay said, his sour experience had nothing to do with the country itself or everything outside of the game. As 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan this week said, it was tough to enjoy it all when you're focused on working.

The Rams head coach was back in his comfortable place this week: back home in Los Angeles as the team goes through a normal week of preparation as they host the New York Giants on Monday night.

"Bottom line is, I like the way that I feel of our preparation, eyes moving forward, chest out, chin up, eyes forward, and let's go be about it," McVay said. "Let's go prepare the right way. Let's have great focus and concentration. Let's have a great energy and an edge in which we prepare and compete with and then let's go be ready to go against a really damn good football team.

"What they looked like in Week 1, we got a great challenge ahead. That's what every week is. We're excited to compete. All we can do is really have a great day of preparation today."

item.title: 5 reasons the Buffalo Bills' Super Bowl breakthrough seems imminent | Opinion
item.description: After an impressive 2-0 start, it feels like the Bills are better positioned than ever to win the franchise's first Super Bowl, writes columnist Nate Davis.
item.content:encoded:
ORCHARD PARK, NY − It would be premature to coronate the Buffalo Bills, a team that hasn’t been fitted for a crown since it won the American Football League title in 1964 and ’65, the two seasons that predated the Super Bowl era.

But after an impressive 2-0 start over playoff-caliber teams like the Houston Texans and Detroit Lions, it sure feels like the 2026 Bills are better positioned than maybe they’ve ever been to capture the franchise’s long-awaited first Lombardi Trophy.

“It was awesome,” quarterback Josh Allen said of Thursday night’s 41-31 defeat of the Lions in Buffalo’s first official game in the new Highmark Stadium.

And the Bills look equally awesome with two wins and 77 points through two weeks, with Allen producing at a historic clip and already responsible for nine touchdowns.

“That quarterback makes things very difficult,” Detroit coach Dan Campbell said following the loss.

Yet Allen may only be a microcosm of a team that appears on the verge of making things very difficult for the entire league – and maybe right up until the final gun of Super Bowl 61.

Here are five reasons that a championship breakthrough might finally be at hand in Western New York:

1. ‘Best quarterback since Elway’

It’s no secret that Allen is among the NFL’s best players, arguably topping the list. Perhaps more critical to his team’s success than anyone else in the league, Allen has already won one MVP award and is pointed directly at a second through two games.

But just how spectacular is he from a historical context? According to one Buffalo legend, Allen is generational.

“Josh is winning a playoff game every single year – and I’ll tell you what, he’s the reason. He’s unbelievable. He’s the best quarterback since John Elway,” Steve Tasker, perhaps the best special teams player in NFL history and a member of the Buffalo teams that reached an unprecedented four consecutive Super Bowls in the early 1990s, told USA TODAY Sports.

“Josh is all of it. Huge arm, can run, really smart. He’s everything in a nutshell. He’s just the right guy at the right time in the right city.”

That was certainly true of Elway, the Denver legend who led the Broncos to five Super Bowls appearances. Of course, Bills Mafia is certainly hopeful Allen won’t have to wait until the final two seasons of his career, as Elway did, to capture the first two rings in Bills history. But, per Tasker, it’s not Allen who needs to raise his level.

“They don’t need anything more out of Josh – he’s scored more touchdowns than anybody in the frickin’ history of the league,” said Tasker, only slightly exaggerating … though Allen has accounted for 300 touchdowns more quickly than anyone in NFL history.

New benchmark: Josh Allen reaches 300 combined touchdowns faster than any QB in NFL history. pic.twitter.com/KsZyZqMeXM

— Pro Football Hall of Fame (@ProFootballHOF) September 16, 2026

Thursday, he also became the first player in league history with multiple passing touchdowns and multiple rushing touchdowns in each of his team’s first two games of a season.

“He is the best player in football,” tight end Dalton Kincaid told ESPN after Buffalo’s takedown of Detroit on Thursday night.

Yet Allen’s intangible value is equally important to the organization.

“He’s so relatable. He’s bigger than life to some people,” Bills GM Brandon Beane told USA TODAY Sports recently. “But in here, he’s gonna treat you, his teammates, anyone, like he’s an average joe – he’s no different than you. I think that’s why his teammates – when he speaks or does something – they follow. He’s a competitor, he’s not gonna hide.

“He’s a driven dude. He’s always thrived on being overlooked.”

Given Allen’s fire, motivation, production and leadership – not to mention the sustained continuity he and head coach Joe Brady, who’d served as Buffalo’s offensive coordinator since the 2023 season, share – the Bills are, almost inarguably, better set behind center than any other team. They just need to support No. 17 lest he try to do too much, as was the case in last season’s narrow playoff loss to the Broncos.

“He would tell you, when you lose those games – the further you go, the worse it hurts when you lose,” Beane said of Allen. “When you get those scars, you don’t want to waste them. You want to use them and the fire, the burning desire to accomplish what is very hard to do.”

2. Joe Brady is the right guy at the right time

Bills owner Terry Pegula made the shocking decision to fire longtime coach Sean McDermott in January. McDermott had revived a once-dormant franchise, leading Buffalo to the playoffs in eight of his nine seasons … but never to the promised land.

After a lengthy interview process to identify McDermott’s successor, Pegula and Beane landed on promoting Brady from his offensive coordinator role – a decision that so far seems inspired and embraced internally.

"He's a real human who guys can get behind and play for," Allen said after Brady was elevated.

EXCLUSIVE: Inside Joe Brady's mission to elevate Bills from winners to champs

A relentless worker affiliated with explosive attacks throughout most of his career, Brady, who ripped off his first in the locker room after the Week 1 win at Houston, has also fostered a more relaxed environment. At times, particularly in postseason, the Bills often seemed as tightly wrapped as McDermott often did, the former coach often criticized by fans for his typically conservative style and game management.

Brady, already the first coach in the history of the Bills to start his career 2-0, will have to truly differentiate himself four months from now to justify Pegula’s pivot. But, for now, his honeymoon phase shows no signs of abating.

“One thing I think Joe has done a nice job of – we’re not throwing everything out, there’s a lot of great things that we’ve done here, but we’re also not running it back," Beane said.

“The energy is very good. … The cake’s still being baked.”

3. DJ Moore’s cascading effect on offense

Buffalo has had a top-10 offense every season since 2020 and never ranked worse than sixth in points scored over that stretch, Allen lording over all of it. That doesn’t mean there wasn’t room for improvement – particularly in the passing game, which had lacked a bona fide No. 1 receiver since Stefon Diggs was traded following the 2023 campaign.

Enter DJ Moore, who was acquired from the Chicago Bears for a second-round pick in March. Apparently not a snug fit in Ben Johnson’s offense, Moore – he can not only get deep but can take a short pass the distance given his explosiveness and quasi-running back elusiveness and power – seems ideal in Buffalo’s attack.

“Their offense doesn’t need to be tinkered with, but better players make you better, no question,” Tasker said. “DJ Moore is a better player, he’s an upgrade.”

And it’s not just Moore’s ability that is literally a game changer. His ability to dictate coverage allows fellow wideout Khalil Shakir, Allen’s top target in 2024 and ’25, to slide to a more appropriate secondary role. Coming off disappointing campaigns a year ago, receivers Keon Coleman and Josh Palmer also looked revitalized in training camp, and that’s largely carried over to the games – Palmer gathering in deep-strike TDs from Allen in each so far, including the game-winner at Houston in Week 1. Lastly, ight ends Kincaid and Dawson Knox also have more room to operate.

“What he does for our offense,” Allen said of Moore, “you can’t really measure it.”

Moore, who caught five passes for 100 yards and a TD in his Buffalo debut, injured a shoulder Thursday night and didn’t return to the game. And while the Bills will miss the obvious impact he’s made for however long he might be out, they should be able to weather his absence in the near term given the other players’ familiarity with the system.

4. A new-look defense

While McDermott’s defense ranked seventh overall in 2025 and finished top 10 in six of his nine seasons, it also came up short all too often in high-leverage situations. A 27-10 loss at home to the Cincinnati Bengals in the 2022 playoffs. The season-ending 33-30 loss at Denver earlier this year. And, of course, the four postseason defeats at the hands of the Kansas City Chiefs, perhaps none more painful than the 42-36 come-from-ahead meltdown at Arrowhead Stadium in the 2021 postseason.

Enter Jim Leonhard, who played four of his 10 NFL seasons as a safety in Buffalo before entering coaching. Now the Bills' coordinator, Leonhard has been associated with aggressive, attacking defenses over the years, including Denver’s in 2025 – though his calm demeanor belies the chaos he’s likely to scheme up as his philosophy takes root.

“Jim is like a calming, confident force,” Beane said. “He doesn’t try to be braggadocious. You wouldn’t even know he played. The guys really thrive on him.”

Confident and relatable but also realistic, Leonhard has suggested it will take two years to fully readjust Buffalo’s D to his vision. But it was sufficiently calibrated in Week 1 to force the turnover that sealed the win. And despite surrendering 31 points to Detroit, the Lions were effectively out of the game before halftime before racking up empty-calorie yards and points.

5. New Highmark Stadium

It’s a lot fancier than its now-leveled predecessor across the street.

“There’s some really nice stadiums, and I don’t think I’ve walked into one nicer. It’s very intentional about things,” Beane said.

Meticulous thought was given to aspects like the locker room, the tunnels, cafeteria, sauna, even hydrotherapy. The canopy that covers most of the seats could create a reverberating cacophony that approximates – and maybe exceeds – the noise at the Seattle Seahawks’ renowned Lumen Field.

RANKINGN 29* NFL STADIUMS BEST TO WORST With an exemption for Bills' new one

Above all, Pegula’s commitment to installing a grass playing surface has been a huge hit among the players.

"This is like being on the inside of a Rolls-Royce, man,” left tackle Dion Dawkins told NFL Network after Buffalo’s preseason opener.

“Across the street was the old Papa Joe's pickup truck, man, and that is gone."

So, too, might Buffalo’s six-decade drought in search of a Lombardi if the Bills’ new approach and new building keep paying dividends at their current rate.

item.title: Makai Lemon knows he has "lots to improve" after minus-5 yards in his first NFL game
item.description: Eagles rookie wide receiver Makai Lemon had a box score to forget in the first game of his NFL career: Against the Commanders, Lemon caught three passes for minus-5 yards.
item.content:encoded:
Eagles rookie wide receiver Makai Lemon had a box score to forget in the first game of his NFL career: Against the Commanders, Lemon caught three passes for minus-5 yards. Lemon knows he needs to do better.

Lemon caught the first pass thrown to him in the flat for a gain of three yards. The Eagles then twice ran a play when Lemon went in motion and Jalen Hurts threw the ball to him behind the line of scrimmage, and on both he was tackled almost immediately, once for minus-three yards and once for minus-five yards.

“Lots to improve on,” Lemon said, via the Philadelphia Inquirer.

So far, the Eagles don't look like they trust Lemon to get open downfield. In addition to his poor showing in Week 1, in the preseason, Lemon also caught exclusively short passes, finishing with three catches for three yards. Lemon knows he needs to show his team that he can run good downfield routes.

“Route details,” Lemon said. “Just making sure I define my routes and assignments.”

Eagles coach Nick Sirianni defended Lemon and said his game was better than his box score looked.

“There’s a lot of things that Makai did in that game that don’t reflect on the stat sheet,” Sirianni said. “We constantly talk about that: What are you doing to help this team win the game, particularly if you’re a skill guy? That might not be able to be seen from the stat book or to the naked eye. What he’s always done a good job since he’s been here [is] blocking, doing the right things, being in the right spots. Obviously the ones that went to him [on Sunday] didn’t equal out to a big yardage game, right? But he did little things to help us win the football game that sometimes are unseen.”

At some point, though, the Eagles need their first-round receiver to make some plays that do show up on the stat sheet.

item.title: Browns legend talks about Shedeur Sanders’ work ethic, progress
item.description: Cleveland Browns QB competition never ends. If Deshaun Watson struggles, Shedeur Sanders might be ready, Bernie Kosar says
item.content:encoded:
For better or worse, all the conversation around teams in the NFL is about their quarterback play, especially with the Cleveland Browns. As one of our readers in DBN’s Feed noted, the stars on the Browns defense needed to do a better job in Week 1 as well, but quarterbacks get the lion’s share of credit and blame in the NFL.

Despite once again sticking his foot in his mouth in a press conference, not as bad as the one right before he got named the starter, Deshaun Watson will take the first snap of the game for the Browns. Many fans and media believe that Watson is on a short leash, with the home opener in Week 3 a dividing line of sorts.

Given how HC Todd Monken has backed Watson, it is possible his leash is much longer than many think, but Shedeur Sanders is waiting in the wings. Cleveland legend Bernie Kosar weighed in on whether Watson will be pulled soon and what he’s seen from the young quarterback that would replace him:

Kosar tends toward the positives when talking about the Browns and players in general. The former Miami and Cleveland star quarterback is often around the team, talking to coaches, players, and club personnel, including filming content for a project of his own during this year’s training camp.

With a report that the Browns will sign Sanders’ former Colorado teammate, WR Jimmy Horn Jr., some believe that is an indcator of a plan to move Sanders back into the starting lineup soon.

Last year, as a fifth round rookie and the third quarterback to start games for Cleveland, Sanders completed 57% of his passes for exactly 1,400 yards, with seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions. The complexities of Monken’s system and Watson’s experience seemed to lead to Sanders chasing in the quarterback competition all offseason, but the veteran struggled mightily, including in presnap process, in Week 1.

Will we get a chance to see what Sanders can do and if Kosar is right about him soon? That’ll be up to Watson’s performance and Monken’s opinion.

item.title: Our defense vs. their offense: Baltimore Ravens
item.description: Previewing the Saints’ defensive matchup in Week 2
item.content:encoded:
The New Orleans Saints currently have the 21st ranked defense in the NFL following their 31-30 overtime loss versus the Detroit Lions in week one action. The Saints gave up 369 total yards of offense while 204 of those came through the air (18th in pass yards allowed) and the other 165 were given up on the ground (28th in rush yards allowed.)

31 points allowed left the Saints tied for 23rd in defensive scoring with the Denver Broncos and Buffalo Bills. Although New Orleans ultimately lost the turnover battle in week one, they still managed to force one (should have been two?) takeaway against Detroit by way of a forced fumble.

Safety Jonas Sanker led the team with ten tackles last weekend while DE Carl Granderson was credited with the lone sack for the black and gold. Vernon Broughton delivered the fumble recovery after a strong punchout on Jahmyr Gibbs.

Baltimore’s offense is second in the league in total offense after their 506 yard outburst against the Indianapolis Colts last Sunday. The Ravens put up as astounding 304 passing yards (5th) and 202 rushing (3rd) behind QB Lamar Jackson.

The Ravens put up the second most points in the NFL last weekend as they dropped 41 on the Colts. Jackson was responsible for two total touchdowns while RB Derrick Henry rushed for three more. WR Zay Flowers was on the receiving end of Jackson’s lone TD pass and finished his day with 150 yards on just five receptions. TE Mark Andrews added another four catches for 49 yards.

Although he did not throw an interception during last week’s contest, Jackson still had one fumble that he lost which led to a four-play TD drive for the Colts.

New Orleans will now attempt to avoid an 0-2 start to the season on the road against a top offense in the league. Even with Flowers, one of Lamar’s top pass catching threats, still questionable to go versus New Orleans (hamstring,) Baltimore has deep offensive firepower and will be a challenge for a young Saints defense to contain.

item.title: Latest news on Lions S Avonte Maddox’s foot injury
item.description: Here’s what we know about the foot injury to Detroit Lions safety Avonte Maddox.
item.content:encoded:
In the midst of the Detroit Lions’ 41-31 butt-whipping at the hands of the Buffalo Bills, they also suffered an injury that they can ill-afford. Early in the second quarter, Avonte Maddox took a friendly-fire shot from teammate Chuck Clark, and eventually had to be carted off with what the Lions called a foot injury. While originally listed as questionable, he was downgraded to out to start the second half.

After the game, Maddox was seen in the locker room in crutches. It’s important not to overreact to that, as crutches can sometimes be more precautionary than anything. However, Lions coach Dan Campbell was not optimistic about Maddox’s status, while also admitting there needs to be more testing to find out.

“I don’t know. Maddox is pretty tough, so when he doesn’t come back, that makes me nervous,” Campbell said. “But I won’t know until tomorrow for sure.”

Detroit is in a tough spot at the safety position. Both starters—Kerby Joseph (knee) and Brian Branch (Achilles)—started the season on the Physically Unable to Perform list and must miss at least another two games. However, both are eligible to return to practice now. And there appears to be optimism at least one of them could be ready relatively soon.

But on the 53-man roster, outside of Maddox, the Lions only have two other pure safeties rostered: veteran Chuck Clark and Thomas Harper. Christian Izien is also an option to drop back to safety, but the Lions have recently shifted him into a significant role as the team’s primary nickel cornerback.

If Maddox’s injury is serious, another option would be to bring up defensive back Nick Whiteside from the practice squad. While he has thrived mostly as an outside cornerback, he got some late looks at safety in training camp and performed moderately well.

For now, let’s just hope for the best, because the last thing the Lions can afford right now is more issues in the secodnary.

item.title: Hunting Explosives: Revisiting the Bears’ Big Plays from Week 1
item.description: Breaking down the Chicago Bears' explosive plays highlighted by Caleb Williams, Rome Odunze, D’Andre Swift, and Kyle Monangai.
item.content:encoded:
There’s a lot to love about Ben Johnson but his focus on hunting explosive plays may be my favorite part of his football philosophy. The Bears logged nine explosive plays (a run of 10 or more yards or a pass of 20 or more yards) in Sunday’s monster victory against the Carolina Panthers. Four of those explosive plays were on touchdowns and the other five led to scores. That’s the most in the Ben Johnson era and a preview of the big things to come this season. We’ll track all of them weekly in this column.

Explosive Play 1.1 – Q1 8:19, 1st and 10 at the Carolina 45. D’Andre Swift carries the ball off right tackle for 32 yards. The possession would end in a TD.

After the Bears turned the ball over on the opening possession, they got things rolling on a scoring drive highlighted by this Swift explosive play. Last year, many of the big runs put up by the Bears were to the right side of the offensive line, so it was fitting to have the first explosive play of the season feed off Darnell Wright.

The Bears huddle here with 11 personnel (1 running back, 1 tight end, 3 wide receivers) and line up in an I-Formation with Cole Kmet as the fullback. Luther Burden starts on the right side of the formation next to Rome Odunze, motioning to the left side before the snap. Darnell Wright kicks his defender off to the right. Jonah Jackson and Garrett Bradbury try to work a double team with Kmet leading into the four hole (between the right guard and right tackle). Bradbury leaves the double team early when Jackson powers his defender off to the right, leaving the center to pick up a linebacker at the second level.

It’s well-blocked and Swift encounters first contact about 6 yards from scrimmage. After that, it’s an incredible display of running from Swift, breaking out of two tackles at the point of contact and quickly juking a third defender, maneuvering back to the middle of the field before getting chased down. Swift gets a ton of the credit here.

Explosive Play 1.2 – Q1 3:01, 2nd and 8 at the Chicago 47. Caleb Williams pass complete deep right to Rome Odunze for 47 yards. The possession would end in a TD.

This is one of those plays I’ve been dreaming about since early last season when it was clear Caleb Williams had a special talent in avoiding pressure. This is a scramble drill success play and one of those aspects of the Bears offense that could take this thing to the stratosphere.

The Bears break the huddle in 11 personnel but split Loveland out to the left side of the formation with Luther Burden. Caleb drops back, looks right, looks left, and flushes to his right. Odunze senses the scramble drill starting and flies down the field with his hand in the air. Caleb throws the ball a little late or short, but it’s either going to be a defensive pass interference or an Odunze catch given the position of the defender scrambling to make back the space.

Odunze reaches over the head and pulls in a highlight throw. While this isn’t the play that is scripted, the scramble drill is something that desperately needed work from last season and something Ben Johnson has mentioned as an area of focus. Early returns are good.

Explosive Play 1.3 – Q2 14:05, 1st and 10 from the Carolina 22. Caleb Williams pass complete deep left to Cole Kmet for 22 yard TD.

This play-action pass elicited an audible gasp-turned-maniacal-laugh from me when it happened. The Bears come out in 13 personnel (3 tight ends!) with the rookie Sam Roush lined up next to Kmet and Loveland on the right side, Jahdae Walker the lone wide receiver to the left. Walker runs a route to the post pulling the boundary defender with him long enough for Caleb to fit a perfect (and I mean perfect) ball into Kmet for the score. Cole’s route starts as if he’s down blocking to the left and quickly heads up field on a TE leak play. The defender does a nice job sticking with him but no defending a perfect pass.

Explosive Play 1.4 – Q2 1:14, 3rd and 11 from the Chicago 19. Caleb Williams pass complete deep left to Kalif Raymond for 28 yards. This was the first of three explosive plays on the drive that ended the half with a TD.

Jump man back at it! This amazing end of the half sequence started with this beauty to Kalif Raymond. The Bears come out in 11 personnel with Loveland lined up tight next to Braxton Jones and three receivers to the right. Luther Burden motions to the left and Caleb takes the snap from shotgun. Caleb pump fakes short to Rome and starts to scramble to his left before firing a jump man pass into Raymond near midfield. Raymond makes a sliding catch and the Bears are in business.

Explosive Play 1.5 – Q2 0:38, 2nd and 10 from the Chicago 47. Caleb Williams pass complete deep left to Luther Burden for 24 yards. This was the second of three explosive plays on the drive that ended the half with a TD.

Two plays later, Williams and Burden connect for a nice little gainer. Sticking with 11 personnel, Loveland is flexed out to the left side with Burden. Loveland runs an underneath route with Burden working intermediate. Burden does a nice job at the top of his stem with a juke before breaking inside with separation. Caleb finds him in rhythm with Burden adding a few additional yards after the catch. Solid pitch and catch.

Explosive Play 1.6 – Q2 0:32, 1st and 10 from the Carolina 29. Caleb Williams scrambles around left end for 29 yard touchdown. This was the third of three explosive plays on the drive that ended the half with a TD.

This was great recognition on the part of Caleb to evade pressure and know that he could get a good gain with man coverage. The Panthers bring only four here but fail to leave anyone to spy on Williams. As the onset of pressure, Caleb tucks the ball to flee the pocket and takes off with his world class speed. Seeing that the coverage was blanketing his receivers in man coverage, the speed of Williams made this an easy touchdown – but don’t discount that there are very few quarterbacks that can reach the sprint speed that Williams has put on film in his young career.

Explosive Play 1.7 – Q3 0:50, 1st and 10 from the Chicago 39. Kyle Monangai runs up the middle for 61 yard TD.

Now we’re just showing off. The Bears take over on downs up 38-31 and score a monster touchdown with Monangai. The Bears use basic 11 personnel with Kmet attached to the right side of the formation. Burden comes in short motion left to right and acts of a lead blocker for Monangai. Raymond scores an excellent block at the point of attack about five yards from scrimmage, allowing Monangai to cut off that block to the right. From there it’s a race to the end zone with Walker providing a…hands up block to slow down one Panthers defender and Monangai using just enough jet fuel to pull off a 61-yarder. This really broke the game.

Explosive Play 1.8 – Q4 8:52, 3rd and 4 from the Carolina 21. Kyle Monangai runs over left guard for 14 yards. This possession would end with a TD.

The Bears come out in 11 personnel and line up in shotgun. They threw a lot from this formation on Sunday. Loveland provides some eye candy with a sprint out from his spot back and to the right of Darnell Wright a second before the snap. It’s a motion that can cause a hesitation from the defenders, useful when handing to ball in the opposite direction as the Bears did here. Monangai takes the handoff from Williams aiming for what looks like the gap between left guard and left tackle. However, Darnell Wright and company collapses everything down to the left and Monangai does an excellent job of cutting back to the middle. Monangai gets first contact around 9 yards downfield, bouncing off a defender and carrying another for an additional five yards. How good is this dude?

Explosive Play 1.9 – Q4 3:47, 2nd and 1 from the Carolina 28. D’Andre Swift runs over right guard for 28 yard TD.

Pouring it on now, D’Andre Swift provides the exclamation point. There’s literally nothing particularly special about this design or even how it’s blocked. It’s 12 personnel with Loveland and Kmet providing key blocks at the point of attack off the right side (surprise surprise, Darnell Wright again!) and the Panthers…poor run fits and maybe a little bit of give up here as Swift just explodes through the point of attack and races to the end zone for his third score and caps the 59 point extravaganza from Chicago. Swift bookends the nine explosive plays for the Bears on the opening weekend, helping him secure the NFC Offensive Player of the Week award.

2026 Explosive Play Count: D’Andre Swift 2, Kyle Monangai 2, and one each for Kalif Raymond, Rome Odunze, Caleb Williams, Luther Burden, and Cole Kmet.

What was your favorite explosive play from the opener? You could make an argument for a lot of them, but right now, I think my favorite is that Cole Kmet TD. Hit up the comments and let me know.

item.title: Washington Commanders vs Dallas Cowboys Week 2: Five Questions with Blogging the Boys
item.description: Two 0-1 NFC East teams battle in Texas
item.content:encoded:
It’s week 2 of the NFL season and the 0-1 Washington Commanders will be facing an 0-1 Dallas Cowboys team on the road at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, TX this Sunday at 4:25 p.m. EDT. The Cowboys had a very disappointing week 1, getting beat in very physical fashion by the Giants on Sunday Night Football.

On offense, the Cowboys are coached by OC and run-game designer Klayton Adams, as well as HC and playcaller Brian Schottenheimer; having preserved the 2025 offensive coaching staff that created the 2nd-best offense in the NFL in terms of yards gained, and the 7th-best offense by points gained. The combo of Adams and Schottenheimer have designed an offense in Dallas that utilizes a lot of play-action, a lot of pre-snap motion, heavy use of tempo, and a very conscious effort to ensure run and pass plays start with the same looks.

On defense, the Cowboys have had a lot more turnover. After fielding the 3rd-worst unit in yards allowed and the NFL’s worst unit in points allowed, the Cowboys made major changes in their defensive unit, headlined by the change at DC from Matt Eberflus to Vic Fangio-disciple Christian Parker, who was formerly the Eagles passing-game coordinator and DBs coach. Parker was expected to run a Fangio-style defense that emphasizes rushing four and dropping the rest back in coverage to limit explosive plays. Perhaps that style of defense works better with the personnel of the Eagles compared to the Cowboys, because the Cowboys only managed two pressures on 20 four-man rushes in week 1.

I asked David Halprin of Blogging the Boys five questions to better understand the state of the Cowboys and what to look for in this game.

1) The Cowboys defense was one of the worst in the NFL last year by most metrics (right up there with the Commanders). What has been done to overhaul it this year and what have you seen from it so far?

A lot was done to overhaul the defense. First was hiring Christian Parker away from the Eagles staff as the new coordinator. With him comes a new scheme that is a base 3-4 but incorporates a lot of 4-3 looks and tries to disguise between the two. So Dallas is incorporating a new scheme, but also a lot of new players. The turnover on the defense had easily over half of last year’s starters gone from the roster on that side of the ball. They also invested heavily in the defense during the draft by using two first-round picks on safety Caleb Downs and OLB Malachi Lawrence. 

So the Cowboys did a lot to change their defense, but the results in Week 1 looked eerily like last year’s team. They were blowing assignments, busting coverages and allowing the Giants offense to dictate the game. They couldn’t stop the run so the Giants just pounded them in time of possession and only allowed the Cowboys offense two possessions in the second half. Parker has a lot of work to do to make this unit serviceable. 

2) What are your thoughts about the Dallas offensive line and what is your assessment of it as a unit?

If the Cowboys were at full strength I would be confident that they could make it work much as they did last year. It’s basically the same cast of characters that were there last year, and the offense was really good in 2025. They are missing their best lineman, guard Tyler Smith, so that hurts them some. Right tackle Terence Steele still seems to be the weak link, especially in pass protection. Left tackle Tyler Guyton had also caused some concern in the past, but he had a strong training camp and held up well against the Giants’ talented pass rush. The running game was an issue last week, so that is also a little bit of a concern this season. Overall, I don’t think the offensive line will be an issue as long as Guyton’s improvements are real and Smith returns healthy after his four-game IR trip. 

3) What are your thoughts on how the Cowboys have been drafting the last few years? As part of this, do you think they’ve been reaching for positions of need in the draft due to being tight on salary cap space?

No, I don’t think the Cowboys are drafting based on need because of salary cap space. They currently have over $20 million in cap space which is among the Top 10 in the NFL. The Cowboys actually do a pretty good job of drafting, that is how they stay competitive while basically eschewing high-priced free agents. Recently, they have had some uneven drafts compared to before when they were on a run of doing very well in the draft. But they are just like any other team, they draft based on a combination of talent, need, scouting reports, etc. There is nothing unusual going on with the Cowboys drafts and overall they do a good job of it, but not quite as good as they were doing for a while. 

4) Who is one Cowboys player on offense and one player on defense that Washington fans probably don’t know much about, but should?

I’m assuming most people know about Caleb Downs, our first-round pick. So on defense, we’ll go with Jaishawn Barham at inside linebacker. A third-round pick this year, he had an outstanding preseason/training camp. Now, with an injury to DeMarvion Overshown, Barham is about to get a lot more playing time. He is a violent player that is a missile heading to the ball. His first week in New York was decent. He did make a few mistakes, but he also showed the talent that should make him a serious player on the Cowboys defense.

On offense, it is tougher because we are basically running out the same unit that played last year, so people probably know many of them. Let’s talk about our TE2 in Brevyn Spann-Ford. He is a big man who definitely helps in blocking, but he has started to show he can be a receiving target, too. Cowboys fans are hoping he breaks out this season. He didn’t do much versus the Giants, but the potential is there. 

5) How should Washington go about gameplanning this matchup on both sides of the ball?

On offense, use RPOs and other misdirection that utilizes Jayden Daniels’ legs to confuse the defense. The Giants did this repeatedly. They also just physically smashed the ball into the line and moved the Cowboys defense. Basically run the ball, then take shots downfield when you can. The Cowboys defense is still trying to get things sorted out, but they just couldn’t stop the run last week. 

On defense, try and take away the run. When the Cowboys can effectively run the ball with Javonte Williams, their offense just opens up and the wide receivers can then get loose and really cause damage. The Cowboys like to stick with the run, so they will continue even if it is not working well. Their offense can then get bogged down and their passing game is lethal, but also susceptible to mistakes. I’m not saying you want the game to be in CeeDee Lamb’s and George Pickens’ hands as a defense, but when the Cowboys can’t run effectively their offense is a different animal. 

A companion article to this with my answers to David’s questions will be linked here when it is available.

Thanks again to David Halprin for taking time out of his day to answer our questions about the Cowboys.

item.title: Scouting the Enemy: Jacksonville Jaguars
item.description: The Denver Broncos host the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday. Here is a deeper look at their Week 2 opponent.
item.content:encoded:
The Denver Broncos host the Jacksonville Jaguars this Sunday for their first home game of the season. The Jaguars were able to dominate the Cleveland Browns in Week 1 and will be a tough challenge for the Broncos this weekend. Here is a deeper look at the Broncos’ Week 2 opponent.

2025 Jacksonville Jaguars Season Review

The Jaguars impressed last season in Liam Coen’s first season as leading the team. They were the AFC South champions and finished with ae 13-4 record. However, they would lose to the Buffalo Bills in in the Wildcard Round.

2026 Jacksonville Jaguars Offseason Additions and Departures

The Jaguars approached the offseason a lot like the Broncos did. Instead of making a lot of big free agency splashes, they opted for continuity resigning players who helped them achieve their success last season. They also restructured a lot of in-house contracts, since they were quite low on cap space.

One addition they made in free agency was inking running back Chris Rodriguez to a two-year deal. Prior to the roster finalization deadline, they traded for offensive lineman Daniel Faalele into the fold. However, a foot injury will keep him sidelined in the Week 2 matchup against Denver.

The Jaguars also lost a handful of quality players this past offseason. Running back Travis Etienne signed a lucrative deal with the New Orleans Saints. Versatile linebacker Devin Loyd made his way to the Carolina Panthers earning a three-year deal worth $45 million. Those were key starters that played a big role in their turnaround last season.

In the 2026 NFL Draft, the Jaguars didn’t have a first-round pick but still added 10 players on Day 2 and 3. Their first pick was a surprise, selecting Texas A&M tight end Nate Boerkircher in the second-round a lot higher than analysts projected him to go. They followed up that selection taking his teammate, defensive tackle Albert Regis in the third round and took Oregon guard Emmanuel Pregnon several selections later who will start at left guard on Sunday against Denver.

Offensive X-Factor: Quarterback Trevor Lawrence

It’s hard to believe it’s Trevor Lawrence’s sixth year in the National Football League. Some may say the former top pick hasn’t lived up to his hype coming out of college. However last year, he put together a rebound season. Lawrence had the best outing of his career throwing for 4,007 yards, 29 touchdowns and just 12 interceptions.

Against the Browns in Week 1, Lawrence was absolutely dominant. He completed 18-of-23 passes for 245 yards and 4 touchdowns and was only sacked once. In the Week 16 matchup against the Broncos last season, Lawrence had himself a big game going 23-of-36 for 279 yards and 3 touchdowns. He also added a rushing touchdown.

In order to defeat the Jaguars on Sunday, Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph is going to have to find a way to dial up the heat on Lawrence and force him into some mistakes. You can’t let him carve you up through the air and extend drives on third down. He’s one of the best in the game, so Joseph and the defense have their work cut out for them.

Defensive X-Factor: Defensive end Josh Hines-Allen

Last year, I had the aforementioned Devin Lloyd as their X-Factor on defense. For this matchup, I’ll be giving that nod to Josh Hines-Allen. A two-time Pro-Bowl player, Hines-Allen boasts over 60 sacks in his first seven seasons in the NFL.

In 2025, he totaled 49 tackles, 12 tackles for loss, 28 quarterback hits, and 8 sacks and was the most productive pass rusher on their defense. Last week against the Browns, he was an impact player posting 5 tackles, two quarterback hits, and 1.5 sacks.

The Jaguars tout a talented front four with Travon Walker playing opposite of him, along with imposing defensive tackles DaVon Hamilton and Arik Armstead. This is a game where Denver’s offensive line is going to have to step up and combat their pass rush.

Quarterback Bo Nix is going to need time to operate in the pocket for their aerial attack to have success. The Broncos’ offensive line didn’t have their best performance against the Chiefs. They need to perform much better and do whatever it takes to slow down Hines-Allen.

How the Broncos can secure a victory over the Jaguars

The Jaguars will be a huge test in Week 2. After being blown out by Kansas City, Denver needs to find a way to win this game.

Last year, Denver struggled to run the ball without J.K. Dobbins in the lineup. I’m hoping they can establish the run and control the pace of the game. You can’t be a competitive offense without being able to run the ball. If they don’t do that—they’re toast.

The Broncos had two turnovers on downs, an interception, and fumble against Jacksonville last December. They have to be on the winning side of the turnover margin on Sunday to have a chance.

Last but not least, they can’t beat themselves. Enough of the drops, enough of the penalties, enough of the missed tackles. Denver needs to get out of their own way and stop being their own worst enemy. Am I confident that will happen this weekend? No, but I’d love to be proven wrong.

Hart’s Prediction: Jaguars 27, Broncos 20.

item.title: Panthers vs Falcons: Week 2 matchups to watch
item.description: Four key matchups as the Carolina Panthers try to beat the Falcons in Atlanta once again.
item.content:encoded:
The Carolina Panthers scored 37 points in their home opener. The offense was clicking and picking up yards and scores at will. Unfortunately the defense let up an absurd 59 points in what ended up as a three score loss. In this space, we talked about the importance of Jalen Coker and Tetairoa McMillan beating the Bears secondary. They did that. We also talked about the defensive front against a strong Bears offensive line. They lost that battle as badly as they can lose it, and that ultimately decided the game.

This week, the Panthers play division rival Falcons who are coming off a game that’s basically the opposite of the one the Panthers just played. Neither they or the Steelers could move the ball against one another, and a defensive touchdown fittingly decided the game in favor of the Steelers. Something has to give in this one.

Devin Lloyd and Bobby Okereke vs Bijan Robinson

The Panthers used the offseason to completely revamp their starting linebacker duo. That did not help them in Week 1 against the Bears. Both D’Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai tallied at least 100 yards rushing, and both found all sorts of space slicing through the middle of the defense. Devin Lloyd had a really rough debut with the Panthers, while Bobby Okereke was largely invisible outside of an early forced fumble. They struggled to do their part to contain the Bears’ one-two punch, and they hardly used their backs in the passing game. Robinson is a much more talented back than either of those two, and he also led the Falcons in catches and receiving yardage in Week 1. If the linebackers play anything like they did in Week 1, it’s going to be another very, very long day for the Panthers defense.

Za’Darius Smith vs Monroe Freeling

Outside of a sack given up to Montez Sweat in the first quarter, Monroe Freeling held up pretty well in his debut at right tackle. He’ll get tested again in Week 2. Za’Darius Smith is operating on a snap count as he works his way back from his midseason retirement last season. In limited snaps against the Steelers, he registered both of the Falcons’ two sacks. He’ll probably be deployed as a pass rush specialist again against the Panthers, and it’s vital that Freeling hold up to let Bryce Young cook.

Tetairoa McMillan vs AJ Terrell

AJ Terrell has long been thought of as one of the better corners in the NFL, but he certainly didn’t look it in Week 1. He was called for a couple of pass interference penalties and should have been called for a third on a deep ball to DK Metcalf. He struggled to keep up with both Metcalf and Michael Pittman. McMillan has a chance to catch him while he’s struggling, and there will be opportunities to pick up some big plays if Terrell maintains his Week 1 form. The Falcons have very good safeties, but there should be room for the receivers to win on the outside.

Bryce Young vs Mercedes-Benz Stadium

Young conquered his Week 1 matchup against Week 1 by having one of the best games of his career in general, and definitely the best game he’s ever had to open a season. Now he’s playing in a stadium that has been home to his best two games in each of the last two seasons. Young closed the 2024 season by accounting for five touchdowns in a 44-38 win to knock the Falcons out of the playoffs. In 2025, Young threw for 448 yards and three touchdowns in another overtime win. Can he make it three straight dominant performances in the ATL?

item.title: Son of former Dallas Cowboys star scores first TDs, steals his dad’s celebration
item.description: Dez Bryant Jr. flashed his dad's celebration twice Thursday night as he scored his first high school touchdowns.
item.content:encoded:
Fans of the Dallas Cowboys vividly remember watching Dez Bryant throwing up the "X" every time he found the end zone.

Bryant's playing days are now over but on Thursday night, Sept. 17, his signature celebration was displayed twice by someone who shares his name.

Southlake Carroll (TX) junior running back Dez Bryant Jr. scored two first-quarter touchdowns as the Dragons jumped out on top of Keller Central (TX) en route to a 35-17 win over the Chargers.

For Bryant Jr., the touchdowns will be ones he will likely always remember as they were the first of his high school career. He finished the night with 14 carries for 77 yards and the two touchdowns.

Bryant Jr.'s first touchdown came with 8:48 remaining in the first quarter as he played through a Keller Central defensive lineman ripping at his face mask and scored from 14 yards out, capping an 11-play drive.

After Keller Central missed a field goal on its next drive, Bryant Jr. and the Dragons offense quickly got going. He capped off a nine-play drive with a 15-yard touchdown run and quickly flashed his dad's signature celebration for the second time.

With the win, the Dragons ended a two-game skid that saw them lose by 30 to North Crowley (TX) and by 21 last week to Allen (TX), two teams ranked in the USA TODAY Sports Southwest Super 15 rankings. Southlake Carroll opened its season with an improbable 34-33 come-from-behind win over Jenks (OK) in the Cotton Bowl.

Next week the Dragons return home for a showdown with V.R. Eaton (TX).

item.title: Bills wideout DJ Moore's shoulder injury vs. Lions reportedly not considered serious
item.description: Moore was originally announced as questionable before being downgraded at halftime.
item.content:encoded:
The Buffalo Bills had a brilliant first half of offense in their Highmark Stadium debut. With one unfortunate blemish in Buffalo's resounding 41-31 victory against the Detroit Lions.

Veteran wide receiver DJ Moore exited Thursday night's game with a shoulder injury, the team announced as it came out of the locker room for the second half.

The injury occurred when Moore lunged for a would-be touchdown pass in the end zone from Josh Allen, only for the ball to bounce off his chest as he landed awkwardly on his shoulder. Moore stayed down after the play and eventually left the field under his own power.

DJ Moore Landed On His Shoulder.

This Does Not Look Good. pic.twitter.com/zmw07oHkt5

— SM Highlights (@SMHighlights1) September 18, 2026

There was hope the issue was minor after Bills head coach Joe Brady checked in with Moore and gave a thumbs up. Moore was later announced as questionable to return with what the Bills described as a "shoulder and stinger," only to be downgraded at halftime.

The injury is believed to be a sprained AC joint that the Bills medical staff believes is serious, ESPN reported. There’s a chance Moore plays in Week 3 against the Los Angeles Chargers, per ESPN.

Moore didn't have a reception and rushed for -1 yard.

The Buffalo wide receiver corps appeared to take another blow when Keon Coleman went down with an apparent ankle injury, but he was back in the game a few plays later.

Moore in his first season with the Bills after a trade last offseason sent him and a fifth-round draft pick over from the Chicago Bears in exchange for a second-round pick. He had a successful debut on Sunday, recording five catches, 100 receiving yards and a touchdown on eight targets in the Bills' 36-31 win over the Houston Texans.

item.title: Miami Dolphins vs San Francisco 49ers injury report Week 2 2026 includes downgrade
item.description: The Dolphins could be without edge rusher Chop Robinson after he is downgraded on Thursday’s injury report.
item.content:encoded:
The Miami Dolphins’ Week 2 injury report is a little more impactful than the report they had heading into last week’s game against the Las Vegas Raiders when everyone finished the practice week available for the game. This week, as the Dolphins prepare to face the San Francisco 49ers, Miami may find themselves without key players.

Linebacker Ronnie Harrison, who played nearly half of Miami’s special teams snaps against the Raiders, remained sidelined at Thursday’s practice after missing Wednesday’s workout as well. He is dealing with a hamstring injury.

Edge rusher Chop Robinson was also out of Thursday practice as he deals with a concussion. He was a limited participant on Wednesday, marking a downgrade in his status and bringing his availability for Sunday into question.

Long snapper Tucker Addington, who sustained a shoulder injury against the Raiders, and rookie tight end Seydou Traore, dealing with thumb and Achilles injuries, were both limited in Thursday’s practice. That matched their participation status from Wednesday.

Safety Dante Trader, Jr., and quarterback Malik Willis were both listed on the injury report but participated fully in practice on Wednesday and Thursday. Trader is dealing with a hamstring issue, while Willis has a toe problem.

The 49ers’ side of the injury report included kicker Eddy Pineiro and wide receiver De’Zhaun Stribling missing practice Thursday. They both also did not workout on Wednesday. Pineiro has an illness while Stribling has an ankle injury.

Running back Kaelon Black, defensive end Nick Bosa, fullback Kyle Juszczyk, tight end George Kittle, and defensive end Keion White were all limited on Thursday. Black was added to the injury report with a groin issue. Bosa returned to practice after a rest day on Wednesday, but is also dealing with a knee injury. Juszczyk has a finger issue, while Kittle has an Achilles injury and White has a back issue; all three were also limited on Wednesday.

San Francisco listed linebacker Dre Greenlaw, defensive end Khalid Kareem, running back Christian McCaffrey, cornerback Upton Stout, and tackle Trent Williams as full participants at Thursday’s practice. Greenlaw, McCaffrey, and Williams all returned from a rest day on Wednesday; Greenlaw is also dealing with an Achilles issue. Kareem is an upgrade from being limited on Wednesday as he works through a shoulder injury while Stout remained a full participant despite an Achilles issue.

Both teams will update their injury reports on Friday, providing a game status designation. The biggest question for Miami will be the availability of Robinson, who is the top edge rusher on the Dolphins’ depth chart.

item.title: Vikings vs Bears preview as NFC North rivals face off in NFL Week 2
item.description: All four NFC North teams finished with a winning record last season, giving the early-season Vikings at Bears faceoff added urgency.
item.content:encoded:
For the second straight season, the NFC North appears to be a dogfight.

This Week 2 matchup, with the Chicago Bears hosting the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, Sept. 20, is no exception.

The Vikings rattled off 29 unanswered points in their comeback victory over the Green Bay Packers in their opener, while the Bears put up a historic offensive showcase highlighted by 59 points scored and 291 rushing yards.

Here’s an inside look at the matchup, along with predictions, an update on Kyler Murray’s health and television information.

Vikings vs. Bears: What’s at stake

A 2-0 start for either team would be an auspicious start in a division that had all four teams finish with a winning record in 2025. It’s the Bears’ first game at Soldier Field since the divisional round loss to the Los Angeles Rams in January. The Vikings won in Chicago last September on “Monday Night Football” in J.J. McCarthy’s first pro start thanks to a fourth-quarter comeback.

Matchup to watch: Ben Johnson vs. Brian Flores

Even before he became head coach of the Bears in 2025, Ben Johnson established himself as one of the best offensive play callers in the league. Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores is certainly a worthy adversary, however.

Johnson will have to keep quarterback Caleb Williams on time as Flores sends wave after wave of blitzers at the mobile Chicago signal-caller. In Week 1, Flores blitzed Jordan Love on nearly 80% of dropbacks. But the Bears’ deadly rushing attack should hinder some of Flores’ aggressiveness. Williams said Flores is elite at creating one-on-one matchups for his defenders by attacking opposing offense’s blocking schemes and is “one of a kind."

Player to Watch: Colston Loveland, Bears TE

Williams will have to get the ball out quickly, and the Bears’ second-year tight end could be a reliable option. Despite the offensive outburst by his team, Loveland had no catches Week 1 against the Carolina Panthers. For the Bears offense to have success against Minnesota, that cannot happen again.

What they’re saying

Johnson on going against Flores: “You like to think he's put everything he could possibly do on tape until you play him next and you realize he hasn't yet. It'll be something new. There always is with him. That's what makes him such a good coordinator. It's a great challenge. It really is. You have a lot of fun on game day. Now the week of preparation is not so much fun, but there's a lot of back and forth that goes into it.”

Williams on playing the Vikings: “We're going throughout the week and you're getting a little less sleep and all of that. This week is not fun during the week.”

Flores on going against Johnson: "What are we getting week to week? It's hard to know. So a lot of the game is adjustments. ... We're gonna have our own game plan to start things off, and it's the same thing on his end. ... It's certainly a chess match. ... It's a lot of fun. And it's a major challenge. That's what we all signed up for."

Will Vikings QB Kyler Murray play?

Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray won the starting job during training camp only to suffer a concussion Week 1 against the Packers. The former Arizona Cardinals QB exhibited the "fencing" position a player who may suffer a concussion assumes following a big hit. Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell did not rule Murray out, and the quarterback was listed as limited on the official injury report entering Friday.

item.title: What hope is there in the Detroit Lions defense?
item.description: What hope is the for the Detroit Lions’ defense after getting pummeled by the Buffalo Bills?
item.content:encoded:
If you were looking for a silver lining in the Detroit Lions’ defensive performance against the Buffalo Bills in their 41-31 loss on Thursday night, you’d have to squint pretty hard to see it. You may have to hallucinate, to be honest. The Bills racked up 446 yards of offense for an average of 6.5 yards per play. For reference, the best offense in the NFL last year averaged 6.2 yards. Josh Allen finished with a 121.4 passer rating, the Bills ran for 203 yards at 5.6 yards per carry, and they punted only twice—once after a dropped third-down conversion and another time after a second-down drop.

In the end, the Bills posted an astronomical 0.44 EPA/play (highest of any game so far in 2026) and 59 percent success rate (second). Whatever the Bills wanted to do on Thursday night, they did.

“We’ve got to clean up a lot of things on defense right now, particularly on the backend,” coach Dan Campbell said after the game.

The understatement of the night.

So where does Detroit go from here? Where is there any semblance of hope on defense after following up a disastrous second half against the Saints with an even more futile performance against the Bills?

Lions coach Dan Campbell was asked what gives him optimism this can get turned around this early in the season.

“I think this front—we’ve got some juice up front, man,” Campbell said. “I think we’ve got a mix of guys that can apply pressure that can stop the run and that relieves a lot of stress on your backend.”

The Lions did apply a fair amount of pressure to Allen on Thursday night. They sacked Allen twice, tallied eight quarterback hits, and finished with a pressure percentage 34.2%—comfortably above the league average. But that hardly seemed to take any pressure off the back end, which was plagued by missed assignment, failed communications, and blown coverages.

“We had a couple of busts—we had more than a couple of busts on the backend for touchdowns in the pass game that really hurt us,” Campbell said. “We had a couple of busts in the run game, too, our fits. We’re fitting the wrong gaps or not where we’re supposed to be. We’ve got two guys in one gap, and (James) Cook is busting these runs.”

Campbell remains hopeful that time on task will help them play cleaner football.

“The more those guys play together, the better they’ll get,” Campbell said. “The more that we really digest what we’re trying to do to opponents or what we feel like we need to do any given week, I think will help those guys, and their confidence will grow and we’ll get better.”

Another reason Campbell has hope is that they can finally dig into correcting the film. Prior to Thursday, Campbell admitted the short week really prevented them from correcting their errors made against the Saints in Week 1. With another set of data points and a long weekend to digest and self-diagnose, they can really start the big adjustments.

“Now we can really digest—okay, this is our two-game snapshot, this is what you are, this says what you are,” Campbell said. “And we can really deep-dive these players, what they do best, what they don’t do or need help in, and we’ll move on from that.”

While there is undoubtedly some truth to the Lions’ defensive mistakes being internal and correctable, it is a eerily familiar refrain from the defensive meltdown at the end of last season. It may be early in the season with plenty of time to improve, but Detroit will need to be much more effective at fixing their mistakes than they were in 2025.

item.content:encoded:
Before the 2026 NFL regular season began, Miami Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley joked that he would aim to give running back De’Von Achane 40 touches per game. During the team’s first game, a 27-13 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders, Achane touched the ball 15 times, including 11 rush attempts for 36 yards.

The Dolphins are expected to be a physical, run-first team, but against the Raiders, that rushing attack quickly disappeared. The team ran the ball 18 times, including six runs from quarterback Malik Willis. The Dolphins’ offensive attack did not operate as expected last week.

Miami Herald writer Omar Kelly shared on Thursday that Hafley is still committed to having the Dolphins run the ball.

Hafley, who is in his first season as Miami’s coach, reiterated he’s committed to fixing that on Wednesday.

“We’ve played one game. I want to run the football,” Hafley said moments before holding a west coast-based practice in Napa Valley. “We have to run the football! That’s all there is to it.”

But is it really that easy?

Based on the four seasons Hafley spent coaching Boston College, there’s little reason to doubt his commitment.

During his tenure as the Eagles coach from 2020 to 2023, Hafley’s teams averaged 36 carries a game and produced 166 rushing yards per contest. In his last season leading Boston College the Eagles averaged 198.8 rushing yards per game, which came off 42.1 carries per game.

item.title: Bo Nix: We're not freaking out about being 0-1
item.description: The Broncos opened the regular season with a dud against the Chiefs, but they're not making too much of one result as they prepare for Sunday's home opener against the Jaguars.
item.content:encoded:
The Broncos opened the regular season with a dud against the Chiefs, but they're not making too much of one result as they prepare for Sunday's home opener against the Jaguars.

Quarterback Bo Nix threw an interception and lost one of his three fumbles in the 31-10 loss to a divisional rival. He was sacked four times in the game and the Broncos only had 176 total yards of offense, which is the kind of performance that might have some wondering if the offense somehow lost its way on the way into the regular season.

On Thursday, Nix said that's not the case in Denver and that the team still believes they're built the right way for success.

"Overall, we're not going to press the panic button and we're not freaking out," Nix said, via the team's website. "We're not starting from scratch or anything. We feel like we're still in a good spot, we just didn't play great by any means, and we've got to play better."

The Jaguars are coming off a more impressive start, although a home win over the Browns is certainly a different degree of difficulty than a Monday night trip to Arrowhead Stadium. Jacksonville won in Denver last season as well, so the Broncos will have to be much sharper if they're going to avoid a week of listening to stats about how few teams go from 0-2 to making it to the playoffs.

item.title: #PostPulpit mailbag: Will the Steelers follow the blueprint against Drake Maye?
item.description: The latest edition of our Patriots mailbag answers questions about New England’s offense, A.J. Brown, and more.﻿
item.content:encoded:
It’s been a long wait in between the New England Patriots season-opening loss and their home opener on Sunday, where they will look to get into the win column against the Pittsburgh Steelers.

So, let’s get into this week’s #PostPulpit Mailbag.

What happened to the deep-ball/explosive-play game vs. Seattle? My impression was that Seattle did a really good job taking away the deep ball, and I’ve seen some All-22 guys say the same. Is that what you saw, or was Maye also missing open guys? If so, why?

More broadly, I suspect we’ll see a lot more teams try to replicate Seattle’s approach against Maye/Pats. Which upcoming opponents are best equipped to do it? My understanding of Seattle’s formula is four-man pressure/stunts + strong run defense despite the light front, versatile second-level defenders, and especially split-safety/quarters-Cover 6 structures designed to take away explosives, with CBs good enough to hold up.

Pittsburgh has the pass rush. Can they replicate the other pieces of Seattle’s formula that gave Maye problems? – Maye The Force Be With You

This is now the blueprint against Drake Maye: Take away the deep ball and force him to take the profits underneath in order to string together long drives.

In last year’s playoffs, teams played two-high safeties against Maye 51% of the time. Against Seattle on Wednesday night, the quarterback faced split-safety coverages at a 57% clip. For three quarters, Maye played the effective but rather boring brand of football he needed to, living in the underneath area of the field to build a 10-0 lead.

Then, he admittedly lost his patience and started throwing downfield, which led to three interceptions and a blown lead.

“You can’t get bored taking what they give you, and that goes for everybody,” Mike Vrabel said.

As Vrabel said, beating these defenses moving forward will start with Maye being comfortable playing boring football. The Patriots also need to straight-up run the football better against lighter boxes, which would force defenses to move the second safety down into the box and open things up downfield for Maye.

They’ll get an immediate test again with the Steelers, as they played every dropback in zone in Week 1 while defensive coordinator Patrick Graham ran a similar strategy against the Patriots last season when he was with the Raiders.

Who takes Brown role while he’s out – XGhost-PepperX

There isn’t a 1-for-1 replacement when it comes to a player like A.J. Brown. It will be a group effort, with the Patriots utilizing multiple players and their versatility.

The biggest two are Romeo Doubs and Mack Hollins. From a production standpoint, Doubs simply needs to be better than his debut in Week 1 (0 catches, 3 targets), while Hollins has already proven his chemistry with Drake Maye. From a skill-set standpoint, both players have the ability to play Brown’s primary X spot, with the other working off of them at the Z spot. Hollins filling in at the X spot could also open the door for Efton Chism III to see the field in a blocking role.

Behind them, Kyle Williams will factor more into the mix due to his ability to play on the outside as well. The Patriots’ offense needs an injection of Williams’ speed, especially now in Brown’s absence.

When Gonzalez covered JSN, he had 1 catch for 5 yards; not covered by CG? 7 receptions for 117 yards & a TD. Even without the 45 yard TD, it was 6 receptions for 72. Should CG have been on JSN more, especially given that Drew Lock focused on JSN for half of his passes and 2/3rds of his yards? – PatsFanFromNH

Having your No. 1 cornerback follow the opposition’s No. 1 wide receiver all game sounds nice in theory. But it’s much more difficult to execute.

Beyond tipping your hand when you’re playing man coverage by having Gonzalez follow JSN across the formation, there is a domino effect in zone coverages when moving your secondary around. Gonzalez would then need to know the zone assignments from wherever he ends up on the field, which would force the other defensive backs to play in different spots and then adjust based on the original movement.

That creates a tall task for everyone when playing a team like Seattle, which moves JSN around the offense quite a bit. Perhaps it’s more doable against a team like Pittsburgh this week, which largely staples D.K. Metcalf to the outside.

Do we think Maye’s shoulder injury is 100% healed? In Week 1, a lot of his deep attempts came out like ducks very similar to how they did in last year’s playoffs. The flea flicker to Brown was particularly egregious – Brown had him beat by a decent margin and that ball was significantly under thrown. Even some of the shorter throws to check downs in the flat came out pretty weak. – Prontocosmo215

Any noticable change to Maye’s throwing mechanics from last year regular season, to post season, to week one this season? Obviously there’s injury claims floating around – Leoa888

I believe he’s healthy and have noticed nothing on the mechanics. I think the biggest issues for the velocity was just Maye playing his first game in seven months and a lack of decisiveness on some of the throws. The flea flicker falls more in the bucket of timing, as Brown takes off downfield before Stevenson flips the ball back to Maye, who then is rushed and does not want to overthrow Brown as the receiver is running out of room vertically.

Hey Brian. Do you think we see a more even distribution of snaps with the running backs this week, considering Henderson seems to be trending towards playing and Rhamondre’s heavy workload last week? – Pat In Agawam

Yes, I would expect it to be more balanced. Stevenson playing 85 percent of the snaps in unattainable moving forward. The Patriots also could Henderson’s big-play ability and just overall speed on the offense 

Last year’s team had great chemistry. Why on Earth would they not try harder to resign Gibbens, Chaisson, & Tonga? All 3 positions lacked depth going into the season. You can’t build chemistry with 1 year rentals every season. And every draft pick they made on Day 3 is garbage. That’s why our depth will be our downfall this season. – VinnieBoombatz71

Tonga got priced out in Kansas City for the Patriots liking. Chaisson wasn’t a fit for what they were looking for off of the field. Gibbens was an interesting choice due to his value and history with Mike Vrabel, but did struggle a bit down the stretch. We’ll see if the depth ultimately improves or costs them.

What are some of the things to be excited about the next week? – sumeetw

Football is back in Foxboro, that’s worthy being excited about. But seriously, a bounce back Drake Maye game would be huge and while A.J. Brown’s injury is a tough loss, I am excited to see who steps up in the wide receiver room (Kyle Williams?).

Will we win a single game this season? Some fans think we’re heading towards 0-17! – tsarsyrup1215

I believe they can. In fact, I’m picking them to do just that this Sunday.

That’s all for this week’s #PostPulpit mailbag. If you have questions you’d liked to be answered next week, submit them online in our weekly submission post on the Feed. Make sure to follow@iambrianhines and @PatsPulpit as well.

item.title: Bills WR Keon Coleman filled in well for DJ Moore against the Lions
